corpus_fellow.text: Corpus Christi was founded in 1352 by two of the town's guilds, after the Black Death. The Old Court is the oldest surviving courtyard in Cambridge.
Our Parker Library keeps some of the oldest books in England, including a copy of the Gospels said to have come over with St Augustine in 597. We let it out very rarely, and never for a sleepover.

corpus_clockman.text: Outside on the corner is the Corpus Clock. No hands, no numbers: just a gold disc with rings of blue light, and on top, a great metal grasshopper eating the minutes.

It's called the Chronophage. Greek for time-eater. Stephen Hawking unveiled it in 2008. It's only exactly right once every five minutes; the rest of the time it lurches, stalls and races, because time feels like that.
On the hour you hear a chain rattle into a little wooden coffin. Cheerful, eh? Underneath it says, in Latin, the world passes away and the lust thereof.
